1.title: Turn off entry bedroom power
1.say: Flip the black breaker toggle for the entry and bedroom to the off position.
placements: black plastic breaker toggle labeled Entry Bedroom → off position inside open gray breaker box in the middle row; in the video: third breaker down on the left side marked Entry Bedroom 1 2
watch_for: If the hall light still turns on, you flipped the wrong breaker toggle.
If the toggle sits in the middle, push it fully to off until it clicks.
1.check_yourself: It should look like the labeled breaker toggle rests in the off position inside the open panel.
1.safety: Touch only the plastic breaker handle with dry hands.

2.title: Take off the wall cover
2.say: Unscrew the four small silver screws from the white rectangular cover. Lift the white rectangular cover straight off the wall.
placements: white rectangular double cover → lifted off the wall beside the white door lock leaving two white switches exposed; in the video: cover over the two rocker switches left of the door
four small silver cover screws → out of the top and bottom corner holes of the cover and into your hand
watch_for: If the cover sticks, you missed a corner screw still holding the top or bottom.
If a switch moves, you are pulling the switch and not just the cover.
2.check_yourself: It should look like two white switches exposed on the wall with no cover.

3.title: Take out the right old switch
3.say: Unscrew the top and bottom silver screws on the right white switch. Pull the right white switch straight out from the blue wall hole.
placements: right white rocker switch → pulled out from the right side of the blue wall box to your hand; in the video: switch on the right beside the white door lock
two small silver mounting screws holding the right switch → out of the top and bottom metal tabs and into your hand
two black wall wires and one bare copper ground wire → left hanging from the blue wall box after cutting free from the old switch
watch_for: If both switches come loose, you unscrewed the left switch instead of the right one.
If the wires spring back short, you cut them too close to the wall.
3.check_yourself: It should look like one white switch remains mounted beside an open blue hole with loose wires hanging out.
3.safety: Keep the power off at the breaker before you touch any wire.

4.title: Connect the green safety wire
4.say: Twist the green wire from the new white switch to the bare copper ground wire. Twist a yellow cap onto the joined ends until tight.
placements: green insulated wire from the new white switch → twisted together with the bare copper ground wire from the blue wall box under a yellow twist cap; in the video: hanging lower right wires below the left white switch
watch_for: If bare copper shows below the yellow cap, the twist is loose and can shock you.
If the green wire joins a black or white wire, you grabbed the wrong wall wire.
4.check_yourself: It should look like a yellow cap joins the green switch wire to the bare ground wire hanging from the box.
4.safety: Keep the power off at the breaker while you twist the wires.

5.title: Join the white wires and cap blue
5.say: Gather the white wires from the wall with the white wire from the new switch. Twist a yellow cap onto the white bundle until tight. Push a second yellow cap onto the lone blue switch wire alone.
placements: white insulated wire from the new white switch → twisted with the bundle of white wall wires under a yellow twist cap inside the blue wall box; in the video: three white wall wires on the left side
blue insulated wire from the new white switch → closed alone under its own yellow twist cap near the wall opening; in the video: short blue wire hanging below the switch
watch_for: If any white copper shows below the cap, the bundle is loose and will lose contact.
If the blue wire is left bare, it can touch other wires so it must have its own cap.
5.check_yourself: It should look like yellow caps close the bundled white wires and the lone blue wire near the wall opening.
5.safety: Keep the power off at the breaker while you join the wires.

6.title: Join black and red switch wires
6.say: Twist the black switch wire to one black wall wire under a yellow cap. Twist the red switch wire to the other black wall wire under a yellow cap.
placements: black insulated wire from the new white switch → twisted to one black wall wire from the blue wall box under a yellow twist cap; in the video: right side black wall wire
red insulated wire from the new white switch → twisted to the other black wall wire from the blue wall box under a yellow twist cap; in the video: left side black wall wire
watch_for: If copper shows below a yellow cap, unscrew and retwist until no bare metal shows.
If a new switch wire joins a white bundle, you used the wrong wall wires and the light will not work.
6.check_yourself: It should look like yellow caps join the new switch black and red wires to the black wall wires.
6.safety: Keep the power off at the breaker while you connect the wires.

7.title: Push in and screw the switch
7.say: Fold the wires gently back into the blue wall hole. Push the new white switch into the right side opening. Drive the top and bottom silver screws into the metal tabs.
placements: new white smart switch body → pushed into the right side of the blue double wall box beside the left old white switch; in the video: to the right of the old switch beside the white door frame
top and bottom small silver mounting screws → through the metal tabs of the new switch into the wall box until snug
watch_for: If the switch will not go in, wires are bunched behind it so fold them flatter.
If the switch sits crooked, one mounting screw is tighter than the other.
7.check_yourself: It should look like a new white smart switch sits mounted beside the old white switch in the open wall box.
7.safety: Keep the power off while you push the wires and turn the screws.

8.title: Put the cover back on
8.say: Set the white double cover over both white switches on the wall. Drive the four small silver screws into the corner holes until snug. Press the lower white button on the right switch to test the green light.
placements: white double rectangular cover → over the left old white switch and the right new white smart switch on the wall beside the door; in the video: covering both switches left of the white door lock
four small silver cover screws → into the top left and top right and bottom left and bottom right holes of the cover until snug
watch_for: If the cover rocks, a switch sits too far out so push the switch deeper.
If the green light is hidden, the cover is upside down so turn it until the holes line up.
8.check_yourself: It should look like a white double cover sits flat on the wall with both switches showing and a small green light on.
